oasis-grades.title: Obstetric perineal injury grades
oasis-grades.teachingPoint: First-degree injury involves skin; second-degree involves perineal muscle.
oasis-grades.textEquivalent: First-degree injury involves skin; second-degree involves perineal muscle. Third-degree involves the anal sphincter: 3a less than half of EAS, 3b more than half of EAS, and 3c EAS plus IAS. Fourth-degree also involves anorectal mucosa.
oasis-grades.limitations: Classification requires examination, including rectal assessment. If the extent is uncertain, seek expert assessment rather than grade from a stylized depth bar.

popq-points.title: POP-Q landmarks and sign convention
popq-points.teachingPoint: The hymen is zero: points above are negative and below positive, in centimeters.
popq-points.populationAndView: Female pelvis, sagittal schematic; anterior left
popq-points.textEquivalent: The hymen is zero: points above are negative and below positive, in centimeters. Aa is anatomically located 3 cm proximal to the external meatus; Ap is 3 cm proximal to the hymen. Their measured positions vary with prolapse. Stage II spans minus 1 to plus 1 cm.

pressure-flow-nomogram.title: Male pressure-flow classification
pressure-flow-nomogram.teachingPoint: BOOI equals Pdet at Qmax minus twice Qmax.
pressure-flow-nomogram.populationAndView: Adult male pressure-flow study; hypothetical dots
pressure-flow-nomogram.textEquivalent: BOOI equals Pdet at Qmax minus twice Qmax. Greater than 40 is obstructed, 20 through 40 is equivocal, and below 20 is unobstructed. At Qmax 10 mL/s, Pdet 40 gives BOOI 20, Pdet 60 gives 40, and Pdet 70 gives 50.
pressure-flow-nomogram.limitations: Applies to the male ICS classification, not female BOO. Low-pressure low-flow does not independently establish detrusor underactivity; dots are synthetic.
